content: Hello! how can I help today?
I live in Texas but worked remotely for a New York company. Do I owe NY tax?

Yes. New York applies the **‘convenience of the employer’ rule**, taxing nonresidents on income earned while working remotely **unless the work was required to be performed outside NY**.

So if your remote status was voluntary, NY taxes still apply.
Can I claim a credit in Texas?
No—Texas has no income tax, so you get no offset. You must file a **nonresident NY return (Form IT-203)** and report only the portion NY considers taxable under its sourcing rules.
What if I also traveled to other states during the year?
You may need to allocate wages across states based on **workdays or W-2 allocation**, and file **nonresident returns** in each jurisdiction. Maintain a detailed work log by location.
Do I need a special form from my employer?
Request a **breakdown of W-2 Box 16 by state**, or use your time records if your employer only reports to one state. Adjust the income manually on your returns if necessary.
